---
title: "Disclosure determined by tier sizes"
subtitle: "3.2 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 9, 22 and 23"
description: "How many pairwise directions are stated for each pattern of tier sizes."
---

Tier sizes alone determine how many pairs are ranked across tiers and how many stay unranked within tiers. Holding unit and tier counts fixed, the distribution weights every nonempty ordered size pattern equally.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Balanced thirty.** Sizes 10, 10, 10 state 300 of 435 pairs (.690), attaining the maximum disclosure for three tiers.
- **Two tiny tiers.** Sizes 1, 1, 28 state only 57 pairs against the balanced maximum of 300; reordering those sizes yields another pattern with the same disclosure.
- **Four tiers.** Sizes 8, 7, 8, 7 state 337 pairs (.775), the maximum for four tiers of thirty units.
- **Balanced twelve.** Three groups of four state 48 of 66 pairs; open **Settings** to edit the size vector or individual tiers.
- **Unbalanced twelve.** Sizes 5, 4, 3 state 47 pairs, below the balanced maximum of 48.

<details>
<summary>Composition weights and tie notes</summary>

The distribution includes every ordered size pattern with at least one unit per tier. Each pattern is counted once regardless of how many ways units could be assigned to it. Quantile rules usually produce nearly balanced sizes, although postrank can merge neighboring tiers to keep equal estimates together. Assessing accuracy requires unit assignments and pairwise posterior error probabilities in addition to tier sizes.

</details>

Standalone: [embed/tier-sizes.html](../../embed/tier-sizes.html), for example `?preset=tiny&theme=dark`.
